title: Starting University Classes Again at Thirty
script: Narrator: [nervous] At thirty, I walked into a university classroom for the first time in nearly ten years, feeling completely out of place.
Narrator: Most of my classmates looked barely twenty, typing quickly on laptops while I still preferred writing notes by hand.
Narrator: During the first week, I sat near the back, worried someone would ask why a woman my age was still studying.
Narrator: [hopeful] I had worked in retail for years, tired and unhappy with the work, before finally deciding to study nursing, something I had wanted since childhood.
Narrator: My family was supportive, but a few relatives quietly asked why I was starting over so late in life.
Narrator: I told them the same thing every time. Late is still earlier than never starting at all.
Narrator: [determined] The first semester was very hard. I had forgotten how to study, how to memorize, how to sit through long lectures.
Narrator: [discouraged] I failed one quiz badly and cried quietly in my car afterward, wondering if I had made a huge mistake.
Narrator: A younger classmate named Vina noticed I was struggling and offered to study together twice a week.
Narrator: [warmly] She never treated me differently because of my age. She simply treated me like someone learning alongside her.
Narrator: Slowly, my confidence grew. I learned to organize my notes properly and to ask questions without feeling embarrassed.
Narrator: By the second semester, my grades improved, and studying finally felt like progress instead of a problem every day.
Narrator: [proud] Now, halfway through the program, I no longer worry about my age in that classroom.
Narrator: I look around sometimes and realize half the room is focused entirely on their own work, not judging mine.
Narrator: [confident] I still write my notes by hand, and nobody has ever laughed at me for it, not once.
